per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: references to labeled data or metadata in documents
per_feature.sage_expl: A broader alternate reading is that the feature responds to technical/metadata contexts containing a `label` field or tag name across markup/config syntaxes, but this is secondary to simply seeing the token `label`.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: structural elements and observations related to data or processes
per_feature.sage_expl: Feature fires at a begin-of-sequence/document-boundary token that marks the start of a new, standalone text segment after unrelated preceding content; it is especially common when the new segment opens like a title, heading, prompt, or other abrupt document start.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: references to software packages, libraries, or APIs
per_feature.sage_expl: Activates on near-literal mentions of the Go module path `github.com/Azure/go-autorest/autorest/...`, especially continuations under that path such as `/azure`, `/adal`, `/to`, or similar import/package references.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: capital letters and formatted text typically found in headings or titles
per_feature.sage_expl: Activates on decorative or prominent document headings containing a letter-spaced all-caps title, often with surrounding divider lines, but the divider lines are not required.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: references to data formats, versions, or structural components in a technical context
per_feature.sage_expl: Feature is currently unsupported by probes; the safest revision is that it may key on dataset-specific corruption where a token fragment is inserted between literal `<<` and `>>` inside otherwise technical text, especially in math/code/biomedical strings such as `BHLH1<<0>>1`, `\<<alpha>>`, or `a_{<<1>>3}`.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: special characters and punctuation in a document
per_feature.sage_expl: The feature fires on punctuation immediately before LaTeX/math content, especially colon or comma right before a `$...$` span or a TeX control sequence.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: code structure elements, particularly related to class and function definitions in programming
per_feature.sage_expl: Semicolon after a generic collection-typed field declaration inside a class, e.g. `ArrayList<T> x;`, `List<T> x;`, or similar container/map fields.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: method names related to getting and setting values
per_feature.sage_expl: Java/C#-style method declaration where `get` begins a camelCase method name, especially after modifiers plus a nontrivial return type, e.g. `private final User getOwner()` / `public static boolean getReady()` / `protected List getItems()`.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: terms related to health conditions or medical terminology
per_feature.sage_expl: The middle/interior region of an unusually long punctuation-only span, particularly within a long hyphen border line rather than on normal prose mentions of dashes or hyphens.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: references to URLs or web links
per_feature.sage_expl: Activates on URL-like slash-delimited web path strings, especially when a host or site/resource name is followed by multiple hierarchical path segments (e.g. example.com/docs/getting-started, forum.net/thread/48291/replies, api.service.io/v1/users/list).

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: assertions or opinions expressed with a reasoning or thoughtful context
per_feature.sage_expl: The feature fires on the discourse marker "I think" when it is used by the speaker to introduce an upcoming proposition/opinion, typically at the start of a clause (e.g. "I think we should...", "I think that's...").

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: references to artists and artistic identities
per_feature.sage_expl: The feature detects the literal substring/token "artist", especially when it appears as a metadata/schema label or identifier in structured text such as JSON keys/values, config fields, and machine-readable records (e.g. type/category/field names like "artist", "artist_id").

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: terminology related to configuration and operational performance
per_feature.sage_expl: The feature may detect corpus-concatenation boundaries: the transition from arbitrary prior text into an unrelated new document beginning at <<bos>>, regardless of domain, with many observed examples happening to be article abstracts, listings, news items, or patent-style openings.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: play-related terminology in a game context
per_feature.sage_expl: Baseball inning-reference syntax: the feature fires on play-by-play/recap phrases where an inning is named with an ordinal, especially in templates like 'in the fifth', 'the bottom of the eighth', 'the top of the ninth', or 'to start the 10th'.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: terms related to legal settlements and agreements
per_feature.sage_expl: Broad polysemantic feature centered on the verb "settle" across two main senses: (1) resolve/decide/bring closure to disputes or questions, and (2) become established in a place or life situation ("settle in/down").

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: topics related to organizational structure and standards in a production setting
per_feature.sage_expl: A narrower subfeature: nouns denoting scalar settings, thresholds, counts, or resource levels when they appear as the object of explicit modification verbs such as increase, lower, cut, raise, or extend.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: specific numerical data and percentages related to statistics and measurements
per_feature.sage_expl: The feature fires on comma-formatted threshold/cutoff numbers that end in ',001' (or closely related bracket-boundary values), especially in policy, pricing, tax, or eligibility text such as '$150,001' or '75,001 units'.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: references to statistical data and research findings related to social issues
per_feature.sage_expl: More specifically, the feature prefers generic statistic-style or habitual-frequency claims in which "someone" is presented as an unspecified recurring victim of harm (e.g. 'Someone is harmed every year', 'Someone becomes a victim daily').

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: instances of individuals expressing opinions or remarks in a discussion or report
per_feature.sage_expl: The feature activates on capitalized surname-like token continuations or uncommon last names in news-style attribution contexts, especially around verbs like said/says/denied after punctuation or quotes.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: instances of standalone "this."
per_feature.sage_expl: A narrower polysemantic component may respond to member-access/code tokens like `this.` at the beginning of a fresh code statement, especially near chunk starts or line/statement boundaries.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: mentions of the letter 'Z' and variations of 'Z' in different contexts
per_feature.sage_expl: Token-boundary wordpieces that begin with uppercase 'Z', especially rare proper names, brands, and technical identifiers (e.g. Zuck, Zillow, ZTE, ZEB1/ZEB2, ZURB, ZSCAN).

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: technical jargon and terminology related to medical or scientific contexts
per_feature.sage_expl: Digits serving as page/pinpoint locators inside formal citation syntax—especially legal or bibliographic patterns like 'at 237', 'p. 128', '347 U.S. 483, 495', or 'supra note 4'—rather than ordinary narrative numbers.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: elements related to React component structure and rendering methods
per_feature.sage_expl: JSX component configuration syntax in opening tags for framework-specific props such as `keyExtractor` and `store`, particularly in React/React Native.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: discussions surrounding the ownership of slaves by Black individuals
per_feature.sage_expl: Historical references to escaped, former, or enslaved people in 18th-19th century slavery contexts, especially abolition/Civil War-era U.S. prose.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: suggestions for improvements or clarifications
per_feature.sage_expl: Sentence-initial anticipatory 'it' in advisory extraposition: patterns like 'It may/might/would be useful/helpful/easier/best/wise/prudent to VERB,' expressing an impersonal recommendation or planning advice.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: elements related to legal or administrative processes
per_feature.sage_expl: May also respond more strongly when multiple spelled-out month-day-year dates appear in a sequence or list separated by commas/semicolons.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: assertions and negations about events or states of being
per_feature.sage_expl: Sentence- or clause-initial contracted "That’s/that's", especially immediately after punctuation, quotes, or a newline; the feature is about the discourse-opening token pattern more than the specific meaning of the predicate.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: positive sentiments related to appreciation and gratitude
per_feature.sage_expl: The feature is especially common in public-facing announcement or community-address discourse where a speaker/group expresses positive sentiment before an infinitive, e.g. 'thrilled to announce', 'delighted to welcome', 'glad to see', 'proud to be part of', 'excited to share'.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: elements related to communication technology and interactions
per_feature.sage_expl: Hyphenated “-wide” compounds, especially forms like “system-wide”/“city-wide” where the feature may target the second piece “wide” or the whole hyphenated construction.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: technical terms and references related to defense contracts and military operations
per_feature.sage_expl: Mentions of named defense contractors and official U.S. defense institutions/agencies, especially entities like General Dynamics, Lockheed Martin, Raytheon, Northrop Grumman, the Pentagon, or the Department of Defense in factual prose.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: specific chemical compounds and their properties
per_feature.sage_expl: Chemical nomenclature containing explicit stereochemical descriptors in or around parentheses near a hyphenated name, especially R/S locant assignments and related stereochemical annotations.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: geographical locations and names associated with places
per_feature.sage_expl: The feature may more broadly detect standalone jurisdiction/place names in reportorial/legal-news contexts, especially around governmental or institutional predicates, whether or not a comma immediately follows.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: phrases indicating the past action of using something or occurring events
per_feature.sage_expl: A surface-pattern detector for the token sequence 'used/use ... to', centered on the past-habitual 'used to' phrase but with some spillover to nearby lexical patterns involving 'used' plus 'to' (e.g. 'used the key to...', 'be used to').

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: phrases relating to the impact of tau pathology in neurodegenerative diseases
per_feature.sage_expl: Bibliographic reference fragments with compact journal/volume/page formatting, especially patterns like Journal 12(4):233-239, Nature 418:133-136, or 6:45-51, 2004.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: geographical locations and their corresponding states or countries
per_feature.sage_expl: Hyphenated or compound-modifier constructions built from a city, comma, and state abbreviation, such as "Austin, TX-based", "Miami, FL-area", or "Denver, CO-trained".

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: key references to research articles, authors, and geographical locations
per_feature.sage_expl: A feature for title-cased multi-word names where a later component starts with "Ph", especially Vietnamese toponyms like "Tân Phước" and "Cúc Phương" including concatenated wiki-style forms.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: descriptions of breathtaking natural landscapes and geological formations
per_feature.sage_expl: The feature responds to enthusiastic scenic-view descriptions, especially landscapes/panoramas described with strong positive adjectives like awe-inspiring, majestic, breathtaking, stunning, or beautiful.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: technical language related to systems monitoring and management
per_feature.sage_expl: Formal technical/admin alert prose about system or hardware health/status notifications—e.g., warnings, notices, or messages concerning servers, storage, backup jobs, RAID, nodes, or cluster health.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: formatting characters or structural elements in documents
per_feature.sage_expl: A token boundary around punctuation in code/math expressions, especially immediately before member-access dots or underscores, as in `uv.x`, `c2.r`, and `_thread_id`.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: descriptions of processes or methods related to organization or efficiency
per_feature.sage_expl: A stronger subcase: instructional or constraining formulations like "in such a way/manner" and "in a way/manner that ...," especially when specifying how something should be arranged, phrased, modified, or organized.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: instances of logging statements in code
per_feature.sage_expl: JavaScript `console.log(...)` call syntax, especially the literal member-access pattern `console.log(` used to print a value or message.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: quantities and measurements related to distance, weight, and currency
per_feature.sage_expl: More specifically, the feature prefers metric distance/mass units written in full after Arabic numerals, with strongest support for forms like 'X meters', 'X meter', 'X grams', and 'X kilograms'; abbreviated units ('g', 'km', 'mm') and written-out numbers are weaker or inconsistent.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: technical specifications and measurements related to hardware components
per_feature.sage_expl: Compact product/specification tokens: concrete numeric measurements, ratings, or model-size strings written in dense number+unit form in catalog/hardware text (e.g., 120mm, 250V 10A, 3.5mm, 7.4V 2200mAh, 4K60, 12MP).

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: statistical measurements and mean values related to age and other characteristics
per_feature.sage_expl: The feature may be mildly polysemantic around average-report language in biomedical prose: strongest on literal statistical 'mean', but with secondary sensitivity to semantically related average-summary phrasing such as 'average' or 'on average' when reporting cohort measurements.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: instances of the word "would"
per_feature.sage_expl: The feature strongly tracks the modal auxiliary token "would", especially when it follows an explicit subject in prose: patterns like "we would", "they would", "it would", "she would".

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: occurrences of package and import statements in code
per_feature.sage_expl: Forum/tutorial prose introducing a Java code example, where the introduced snippet begins with a `package <java-style-name>;` declaration (e.g. 'I have the following class:' or 'the main class as follows:').

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: references to rural areas and provinces
per_feature.sage_expl: Words for subnational or non-urban geographic regions, especially the tokens 'province/provinces', 'provincial', and 'rural'.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: terms related to speed and rapidity, particularly the word "fast" in various contexts
per_feature.sage_expl: The feature primarily detects the literal token 'fast/Fast', especially when it functions as an adjective or as part of a fixed multiword expression/name (e.g. 'fast food', 'fast-paced', 'fast-flowing', 'Fast forward', 'Fast Track', 'Fast and Furious'). It is much less about the general concept of speed than about this specific lexical item in phrase-like contexts.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: references to user instructions or commands related to technology
per_feature.sage_expl: South Slavic oblique personal pronoun forms built on nj- (njega, njemu, njoj, njih, nje), especially after prepositions, likely firing on an internal subtoken boundary within the pronoun.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: references to user interface components in programming
per_feature.sage_expl: Android/Java import statements for UI-related classes specifically from `android.widget` (including widgets like `Button`, `ListView`, `TextView`, and likely `Toast`), rather than imports from other Android packages.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: function declarations in programming contexts
per_feature.sage_expl: Start of a C/C++ function declaration/definition with return type `void`, with strongest activation when `void` appears at the beginning of a new line and especially when separated from prior code by a just-closed block.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: requests to avoid editing or modifying content
per_feature.sage_expl: Boilerplate warning/disclaimer language in technical text that forbids modification or reliance, especially generated-file notices like "DO NOT EDIT".

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: references to the OpenAPI specification and its components
per_feature.sage_expl: The feature fires on the exact token/segment `openapi` when it appears as a package component in dotted Java/Kotlin-style names, especially IntelliJ references such as `com.intellij.openapi.*`.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: phrases and structures that indicate comparative or relational contexts
per_feature.sage_expl: Comma + 'with' introducing a non-argument supplementary clause that gives an accompanying state/process, often with a participial or predicative complement ('..., with bacteria being transmitted...', '..., with the extracellular side showing...').

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: parenthetical information and dates related to personal details
per_feature.sage_expl: Genealogy-style appositive person descriptions combining a named individual with nearby kinship or identity metadata, often via commas or parentheses—e.g. 'Thomas, son of Edward and Anne' or 'Gladys (Oakwood) Sanders'.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: terms related to costs and expenses
per_feature.sage_expl: The feature may extend to business/accounting terminology built around the word "cost," such as "cost centers," "cost allocation," "cost drivers," and related finance/operations phrases.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: phrases indicating opportunities or chances for action
per_feature.sage_expl: A complement-taking construction with nouns like 'chance', 'opportunity', or 'time' followed by 'to' or 'for', expressing an opening/availability for an action or event (e.g. 'chance to help', 'time for reflection').

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: genetic terminology related to inheritance patterns and chromosome characteristics
per_feature.sage_expl: Genetics/chromosome inheritance terminology, especially sex-chromosome vs autosomal concepts such as heterogametic/homogametic, autosomes, sex-linked/X-linked, and chromosomal inheritance.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: HTML or XML tags and attributes
per_feature.sage_expl: The specific HTML boundary `attribute="value">`: the closing double quote immediately followed by `>`, marking the end of a start tag and transition into text/newline.

per_feature.neuronpedia_expl: the presence of mathematical notation and symbols
per_feature.sage_expl: Possible LaTeX-specific subfeature: opening parenthesis introduced by TeX-style constructs such as \left( or after decorated symbols/macros, rather than plain prose use of parentheses.
